title: A virtual element method for Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity
summary: Considering the computational advantages of virtual element methods (VEM), this work employs a conforming VEM for the numerical approximation of the Kelvin--Voigt model of viscoelasticity. For clarity and simplicity, we focus on the primal formulation. The spatial discretization is carried out using the virtual element method, while the temporal discretization is handled via the {second-order Crank--Nicolson} scheme.
